📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

In a recent development, founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, debuted in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website notes the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped.

Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the organization since it unveiled a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games released, and underperformance among substantial releases. Ubisoft remarked in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months.

Ubisoft did have a significant hit earlier this year with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, but that wasn't enough to prevent post-launch layoffs at developer Ubisoft Singapore. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot stated today that "Q2 exceeded our expectations, driven by the continued success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and solid contributions from our broader portfolio.".

Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (486 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness).
  • Sources indicate that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store.
  • "Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation people claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

Sources indicate that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

Sources indicate that the lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

According to recent reports, interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game launches.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East Latest York.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

It has been revealed that it's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox Upcoming Zealand trick for eager players to try.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I've accepted that Arnold Schwarzenegger can probably do things at 79 that would put me in physical therapy. Still, watching him take time from his busy 2026 movie schedule to hoist an enormous Christmas tree overhead while dressed as Santa Claus made me do a double take. The moment comes from a new Santa Schwarzenegger holiday ad, which follows the action icon through New York City in a Santa suit as he dodges the paparazzi. Somehow, he winds up helping a family load a tree onto their car. I suspect some movie magic made that lift possible, but seeing Arnold casually handle an entire evergreen is pretty funny. It also has me wondering: What's it like doing stunts at his age?

The Santa clip landed on Arnold's Instagram just days after the former governor got candid about what action scenes feel like at his age. During his November 11 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Schwarzenegger discussed the possibility of returning to Predator, Commando, and Conan the Barbarian. Kimmel brought up King Conan, which would follow his famous warrior as an older ruler whose reign is threatened. When the conversation turned to the demands of filming that kind of movie, Arnold admitted the years have made a difference:.

I tell you one thing, to do all this action and the sword fighting and horseback riding, and all this stuff is not as easy anymore today than it was 40 years ago…. Well, you get older and you slow down a little bit, right?

Industry observers note that four decades ago, Schwarzenegger swung swords and ran through jungles. I'd imagine climbing onto a horse in full costume feels a little different at 79. Of course, he wasn't about to let a serious observation about aging ruin a perfectly good joke. He swiftly followed up with a line that had me laughing:.

Recent findings suggest that no, not very much. But still, I'm now at an age where it takes me an hour and a half to watch 60 Minutes. Unbelievable, I think. Things are really slowing down.

In a recent development, that's a pretty fantastic old-man joke. The timing is even better when you remember this is the same guy currently showing up in Amazon’s holiday commercial looking capable of bench-pressing a Christmas tree. Kimmel also commented on how muscular Schwarzenegger still is, which led to some playful back-and-forth between the two. Even the Terminator is still perfectly comfortable being the butt of his own jokes.

A post shared by Arnold Schwarzenegger (@schwarzenegger).

Industry observers note that schwarzenegger isn't pretending he can simply pick up where he left off in 1986, either. He's spoken about how a potential King Conan would acknowledge the character's age, with Conan having spent decades on the throne before facing a threat to his kingdom. That's an idea I can get behind. CinemaBlend has already covered his updates about possible Predator and Commando sequels, although he told Kimmel he was still waiting to see finalized scripts.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the Christmas tree is a nice bit of promotion for The Man with the Bag, Schwarzenegger's fresh Prime Video holiday movie with Reacher star Alan Ritchson and Awkwafina. In it, he plays Santa, who recruits a thief to recover his stolen bag of presents. The film arrives December 2 for anyone with a Prime Video subscription, marking his return to Christmas comedy 30 years after Jingle All the Way.

As for that tree lift, I'd love to see some behind-the-scenes footage before giving Arnold full credit for the feat. But the man seems to be having a blast playing Santa, and I hope he keeps finding excuses to do action scenes. Maybe someone can make him a really comfortable saddle for King Conan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the day before the Governors Awards, a studio executive who had attended the past few years told me that she often found herself crying at the star-studded gala. The annual awards ceremony, held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, is often an emotional event, with honorary Oscar statuettes bestowed on influential figures in the film industry. A tribute to Michael J. Fox in 2022 and a posthumous honor for Quincy Jones in 2024 left many guests misty-eyed.

At Sunday’s gala, that teary-eyed trend continued when Glenn Close finally got to hold her own Oscar, after eight nominations without a win. Others got emotional when Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, the independent producers from Killer Films, were honored for their tireless work making boundary-pushing and challenging movies. And when Floyd Norman, the 91-year-old artist who was the first Black animator to join Walt Disney Animation Studios, thanked his wife and five children, the crowd cheered along with him. Even though honoree Ridley Scott couldn’t attend, he dedicated his award to his late brother Tony Scott in a video message. “It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” remarked Matt Damon in his remarks for Scott, who has been nominated for four Oscars but has never won competitively.

The presentation of honorary Oscars is often a way to correct Academy Award history, recognizing those who have been overlooked but deserve to be honored for their lifetime of dedication to storytelling and film. The Governors Awards ceremony is also a major stop on the Oscar season campaign trail, with a room packed full of stars and filmmakers from the year’s contenders.

Sources indicate that this year that meant a surprising number of couple contenders, including Monica Barbaro and Andrew Garfield (who both star in Artificial), Carrie Coon and Tracy Letts (The Liberation), and Zendaya and Tom Holland. Though Zendaya and Holland arrived together and walked through the Ray Dolby Ballroom as a pair, they actually sat at different tables—Zendaya at the Dune table, with Timothée Chalamet and director Denis Villeneuve, and Holland at the Odyssey table, with director Christopher Nolan. Chalamet also made a date night out of the event, bringing Kylie Jenner with him.

The room held a mix of A-list Hollywood stars, like Tom Cruise (in support of Digger), Julianne Moore (The Debut), and Charlize Theron (The Odyssey), and breakout filmmakers of the year, like Obsession’s Curry Barker, La Bola Negra’s Los Javis, and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman.

Another breakout of the season, La Bola Negra star Guitarricadelafuente, has been busy promoting the film as both an actor and a musician, having written the original song “La Nieve.” I wondered if he was exhausted from doing double duty. “I’m not tired,” he remarked with a smile, raving that he had enjoyed meeting many of the other songwriters in the race this year.

All four of the presenters who handed the Oscars to the honorees are also in the Oscar race this year. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star Mahershala Ali honored Norman; Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich honored his Dangerous Liaisons costar Close; Julianne Moore, teaming up with Todd Haynes, honored Vachon and Koffler; and Damon, the star of The Odyssey, honored Scott.

In a recent development, as Close took the stage to accept the award from Malkovich, she wiped tears away from her eyes. The star of films including Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, The Wife, Albert Nobbs, and The Big Chill spoke about being raised in a religious cult and how, in her childhood, animated films were her only escape. She also spoke about being nominated for eight Oscars over her career, insisting that it didn’t phase her not to emerge victorious. “As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not,” she claims. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room.”.

It has been revealed that she wrapped up her speech with a strong statement against AI. “The craft of acting and of great storytelling has never been more vital to the existence of our fragile, violent, but capable-of-transcendence species,” she said. “We are not machines. We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation.”.

Vachon and Koffler have been making indie films through Killer Films since 1995, championing movies like Far From Heaven, Boys Don’t Cry, Kids, Carol, and Still Alice (which won Moore her Academy Award for lead actress). They dedicated their awards to the many people they’d worked with over the years, some of whom were in the room. “We have walked into propellers with you and what has resulted is usually a piece of work that has touched somebody. Sometimes it’s seen by millions of people and sometimes it’s seen by tens of people,” mentioned Vachon. “But our movies came to life and made it to the screen because writers and directors trusted us with their stories and actors knew we were creating an environment that enabled them to give their best performance.”.

Sources indicate that many of the honorees spoke about the mentors and industry giants who had helped them along the way. Close noted she’d promised her World According to Garp director, George Roy Hill, that she’d thank him if she ever won an Oscar. “I never got the chance to thank the man who put me in my first movie. Now I can,” she said, holding her statuette up high. Scott, the director whose prolific career output includes Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien, Blade Runner, and The Martian, told a story in his video message about making his brother star in his very first project, the 1965 short film Boy and Bicycle. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony,” Scott said of his brother, who died in 2012. “His great work would certainly have earned this recognition.”.

#51444. 'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (699 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time.
  • Recent findings suggest that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox.
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Recent findings suggest that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

According to recent reports, no matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar states that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.".

PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

While PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

According to recent reports, in the post, Rockstar also announced that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

That's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar says that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

Recent findings suggest that again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the company hasn't explained why that is.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.
  • Sources indicate that the cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

Sources indicate that the cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and mentioned the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of new updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age upgrade, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

Recent findings suggest that "The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

It has been revealed that itâs very easy in 2026 to just assume your game is saving all the time. Itâs rare to play a game that isnât going to put you right back where your character was standing if you quit, even and especially with open-world titles. But Rockstar wants you to commit to every GTA 6 session, and that might mean choosing when and where you want to call it quits for the night.

Grand Theft Auto 6 does have an auto-save system, something the series started including with GTA 4 on the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, but it might not work as often as you think or hope. Players who decide to take a break from the main story missions and earn some money or do other optional things, only to shut their consoles off, have been waking up this morning to find that none of what theyâd accomplished in the ten, fifteen, or sixty minutes prior to calling it a night had been retained.

So let this serve as a public service announcement that you probably should not rely on auto-save with GTA 6, as well as an explanation for what you should do when youâre ready to stop puttering around in Leonidas for the session.

In a recent development, the game does have auto-save, so on a broad enough time frame, your progress will be saved without you needing to do anything. But it depends a little bit on what you choose to do with that time. Based on our testing, GTA 6 will save after main story missions and larger side missions. Getting your neighbor some rum does not automatically save the game, but successfully stealing a car from the impound lot for Cal and escaping the cops as part of the main story campaign does.Â.

According to recent reports, but this does mean that if you decide you want to cool down after a main mission and knock over a liquor store or do some thoughtful errands, you should not be relying on autosave to do its thing. The game also just does not auto-save during missions, period, so anything you do between starting a mission and finishing it will not be retained if you turn off the console or lose power.

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what upcoming horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

Recent findings suggest that it is time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5. Did we not say goodbye literally yesterday, when I installed a mod named Farewell Los Santos, and there was even a video and everything, and we put Komm Susser Tod over it?

No. 53 mods ago, I told you, the reader, that my mission here was to either mod GTA 5 into a version of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PC, or break the game trying. Admittedly, my mission was successful: GTA 5 is actually better than GTA 6 now. But that means only one thing: as a final send-off, I can think of nothing better to do than finally fulfil the other potential outcome of our initial gambit. It is time to break GTA 5 entirely.

I have installed Fences Network, Simple Weapons Saving, Dragon Trainer V – How to Train Your Dragon Mega Pack, Empire: Singleplayer Overhaul, In The Hood (Gang), BodyGuard Menu, Addon Car Spawner Plus, Rideable Sandworm, Buckme Money App, Realistic Tactical Loadout - GTA VI Inspired Visible Weapon Carry, Pickup, & HUD System [Legacy & Enhanced], Gang Mod Respect System, Los Santos Collapse [Legacy & Enhanced] Zombie mod, The Last Heist - An ending for GTA V [Story Mod | 10 Missions], Real Life Mod [Legacy], Raul's Revenge DLC, Warzone Infil, RageHandlingEditor (RHE) [Legacy & Enhanced], On foot radio (with animations and headphones customization), Keep Right, and Ending C with M83 Midnight City.

In a recent development, in other words, everything that was on the front page of GTA 5 Mods dot com's scripts section when I loaded it up this morning. This took some doing, involving quite a lot of faffing around with OpenIV and myriad .rpf packages to get everything installed.

Would you be surprised to hear (you will not be surprised to hear) the game does not start anymore? GTA 5 has gone to that great sleep that awaits us all. Oh, don't get me wrong: it will boot to the main menu, but try to resume a game or start a new one and GTA 5 will, valiantly, spend about a minute and a half with its cogs audibly grinding against another before simply dumping you back at your desktop—no fanfare, no error message, just swift death. After enduring 53 other mods without completely breaking, it rests now in the great beyond.

I can't wait to do this to GTA 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that welcome to Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, a collaborative multimedia project in which Lifehacker, CNET, ZDNET, and Mashable harness the power of our product testing laboratory and our editors' expertise to offer the best gift-buying recommendations possible. In this episode, we're talking televisions.

I recently did a deep dive into TV development history, checked out what was on shelves for 2026, and I concluded that the best gift TV you can give this year is, actually, a pair of sunglasses. The XBX by XReal video display glasses are basically a TV you can shove in your pocket. Check them out:.

I looked past traditional sets for a couple of reasons. First, because as much as we all love a great show or movie, who actually buys someone a TV set as a gift? More importantly, there's the nature of television itself. Since it was invented in the late 1920s, television quality has been measured by how big the screen is and how clear and bright the picture is, but in 2026, a nothing-special 4K television delivers an image that is pixel-invisible to a typical viewer, and most of us don't have living rooms big enough to need a display bigger than 65 inches. I think the innovation in the space is going to come from the form factor and the use case, and what better form factor is there than a pair of sunglasses?

It has been revealed that these glasses deliver the equivalent of a 142" TV viewed from across the room. It's hard to compare resolution to traditional TVs—technically, the display is 1080p in each eye, but because the TV is just millimeters from your eye, it looks much clearer than that. The peak brightness is 1,600 nits, bright enough for most rooms, and there's a totally opaque shield if you need it. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz. They support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling, offer billions of colors, and it's all in a package that weighs only 62 grams.

According to recent reports, then there are the use cases. It can act as a separate monitor for your computer; you can watch a different show than your roommate without bothering them; but most of all, these are great for flights. There is no situation in life that calls for a massive screen TV more than a cross-country airplane flight. Slip these on with a pair of headphones, and you can fly to Boise in your own private, virtual theater.

Industry observers note that they plug right into any device that supports USB-C video, there's no battery to remember to charge, and they cost less than $300. In other words: They're the perfect TV gift for the holidays, even if they aren't technically a TV.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christopher Nolan notes there are plenty of deleted scenes from The Odyssey, but that we won't be seeing them anytime soon.

According to recent reports, "There’s a lot of deleted scenes scrumpled up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see," Nolan told The Independent. "I don’t really believe in director’s cuts. I want to stand by the film that goes out. As a writer-director, I try to do a lot of that weeding out. There aren’t many scenes that were shot.".

Continued Nolan: "On a film like this, to spend a day shooting something on top of a mountain or in the rain or on a boat or whatever that isn’t gonna be in the film, I would really rather not do that. And so I wanna stand behind the cuts of the films that are put out there.”.

Industry observers note that the film hit theaters on July 17, stayed on premium large format screens until September 30, got another release in October, and will have one last IMAX 70mm release in December. It earned over $1.8 billion at the global box office, which officially makes it the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time.

According to recent reports, the nearly three-hour-long movie was finally released on premium VOD, 4K, and DVD this week... and we're sad that there are no special deleted scenes included in the release. We can only imagine that a Nolan-style director's cut would put the film up to four, or even four-and-a-half hours, and yet I'd probably still go out to see that in 4DX.

Lil’ Kim Takes The Spotlight—With A Symphony

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1476 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When you hear the name Lil’ Kim, a variety of images come to mind.
  • In a recent development, today she’s less interested in being in the spotlight and more focused on raising her 12-year-old daughter, Royal Reign.
  • This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you hear the name Lil’ Kim, a variety of images come to mind. She’s forever known as the force of nature from Brooklyn who turned the music industry on its head when she entered the scene, and her bodacious lyrics and unique fashion sense have kept her as a source of inspiration on your favorite designer’s mood board ever since. On November 18 and 19, to celebrate the music that cemented her icon status, Lil’ Kim will perform in front of a symphony orchestra at the Kings Theatre in Brooklyn, not far from her humble beginnings.

In a recent development, today she’s less interested in being in the spotlight and more focused on raising her 12-year-old daughter, Royal Reign. In between practices for her performances, Lil’ Kim spoke with Vanity Fair to reflect on her career, how she spends her days, and her standout looks.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: What do you remember about putting your debut album, Hard Core, together?

Sources indicate that lil’ Kim: I remember Biggie and Un [Lance Rivera], who was the label owner that we had. I watched Un build a record label called Undeas, which [stood] for “Un ideas,” and then he finally sold it to Atlantic Records. At the time, we didn’t know the process, but we became Undeas-Atlantic. I remember Biggie having the idea of how he wanted my album to be red, and he explained it to me and Un. I was able to write according to how his idea was to present me, because when they met me, I was who I was—in high heels, jeans, motorcycle jackets, and furs at 13.

Portrait of members of R&B group 112 and rappers Notorious SUBSTANTIAL and Lil’ Kim circa 1996.

That’s incredible. It sounds like your fashion-icon status started very early. Was there anyone that you looked to back then? What inspired you to dress that way?

My mom was a big inspiration to me when it came to fashion, and so I looked to her for a lot of things. I used to wear her mink coat. She used to wear big sunglasses with her fur coats, with the diamonds and jewelry. She was always taking vacations and I would see her pack her stuff, and she would always have the cutest outfits. They were all matchy-matchy. It’s funny because she would have her outfit to go play tennis in and her outfit would match her tennis racket. So when I bought my big house, I bought a Chanel tennis outfit and I bought the racket to match it, because of my mom.

According to recent reports, I love that. Do you keep up with tennis or specifically the ladies in tennis?

No, I haven’t in a while, but, of course, you know, Serena and Venus were like my heroes.

Well, maybe we need to see you on the court one day.

Recent findings suggest that I know. I’m pretty sure I’m rusty, but I like to get out there, though. I used to beat my cousin’s butt back then.

How did the symphony performances come about?

My agents called me and they’re like, “Kim, what do you think?” And I was like, “That’s a freaking awesome idea.” I love performing with bands. And so I imagine that it could be very similar, if not very close. And I thought this could be something really different for me. Sometimes I even listen to classical music. I don’t have to know who the artist is, but I just put on a station and let it flow.

Do you have a favorite song from Hard Core?

According to recent reports, I love “Queen Bitch”; it’s my favorite song. It’s still my favorite to perform. And “Crush on You.”.

Salma Hayek, Donatella Versace, Pamela Anderson, and Lil’ Kim at Versace’s spring/summer 2001 fashion show.

When it comes to fashion, you’re obviously on everyone’s mood board, from stylists to designers, so how crucial was fashion for you as part of the Lil’ Kim persona?

It has been revealed that I just was being myself, honestly. When I first met Biggie, I was coming from my after-school job at Bloomingdale’s. I was probably 13 or 14 at the time, and they would let the teenagers work there.

Recent findings suggest that but I had on a motorcycle jacket and high heels. And one of my best friends told Biggie, “You know, my girl can rap,” because we knew he was rapping around the way. And he was like, “I heard you can rap.” And I just laughed. He was like, “Yeah, see, I knew you didn’t know how to rap.” He was very condescending. He knew how to get you to do what you wanted to do, because I was really shy.

Recent findings suggest that and then I started rapping, and he was blown away because I had on high heels. No one had ever seen someone just bust a rap in high heels. When Biggie, Un, and Jacob York started really talking to me, they didn’t want to change me because that was just what they were so blown away about. That was just who I was.

Do you think people ever misunderstood the way you presented yourself?

Recent findings suggest that to be honest, I never really felt misunderstood by my hardcore fans—the kids my age and the younger kids, they totally got it. I think that’s why I had such a cult following and there was such pandemonium about me when I came out. They understood me. I think it was the older people and the politicians, those are the people who I think misunderstood me.

What did you think of the midterm elections and all of the women who broke barriers in the Senate and gubernatorial offices?

I’m going to be honest with you, I stay away from politics.

It has been revealed that are you keeping up with all of the changes within fashion today? When I listen to your music, you’ve mentioned so many designers and houses, and since then the creative directors have changed. Are you following all of the changes within fashion and seeing how you’re still a part of the conversation?

Sources indicate that that’s what I’m trying to say. As a fashion icon, if you really her, and I’m considering myself really her, that’s never gonna change. That’s never going to change. I might put on a fur coat that my stylist or myself will get asked about, because I style myself a lot. And I was styling myself then.

Lil’ Kim and daughter, Royal Reign, on June 16, 2016, in New York City.

What has motherhood been like for you?

Extremely rewarding. My daughter’s with me all the time. This world is so cruel and so evil; it’s so different. She’s my safe haven. I feel the extra need to keep her safe.

What does a regular day look like for you?

Recent findings suggest that lately, I’ve just been really getting into myself. I get up and go have a little spa day. I might take my daughter to go do whatever she wants.

Singer Mary J. Blige with Diana Ross and Lil’ Kim at the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards on September 9, 1999.

How do you feel that we’re still talking about your MTV VMAs look in 1999?

I think it’s iconic and I love it. I love when they bring that up, because it was a fun day and it was so good to see people’s faces when they saw my outfit.

Are there any other looks that don’t get as much love as you wish that they did?

It has been revealed that I don’t know, because most of the looks that I love, they get the love. There’s a look when I was on the cover of Nylon magazine and I had the teddy bear dress on; that’s one of my favorite looks. The Louis Vuitton look is one of my favorite looks; I love that look. A lot of the Chanel looks and the Versace and the Chanel in the hair.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

Industry observers note that "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.".

It has been revealed that feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it.".

Feder, who presently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

"A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder mentioned. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay.".

Feder views gen-AI simply as newly introduced technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder remarked of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected.".

According to recent reports, there's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

It has been revealed that some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the manufacturer is currently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

Blizzard suspends World of Warcraft: Forever gold exploit abusers, puts trading blocks on their accounts and removes ill-gotten funds for good measure

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • Recent findings suggest that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.
  • It has been revealed that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

Recent findings suggest that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

It has been revealed that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

In a recent development, "As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

According to recent reports, it goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

Recent findings suggest that "Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

In a recent development, "Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

In a recent development, the post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

Inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

#51427. Stacey Abrams in Conversation With Ta-Nehisi Coates

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4128 w)

Stacey Abrams in Conversation With Ta-Nehisi Coates

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4128 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When I first met Stacey Abrams in 2015, she passed on to me the message that she was then passing on to anyone who’d listen: Someday soon, Georgia would be blue.
  • The following conversation has been lightly edited for length and clarity.
  • Industry observers note that ta-Nehisi Coates: My recollection of our first meeting goes back to 2015, when I was promoting Between the World and Me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When I first met Stacey Abrams in 2015, she passed on to me the message that she was then passing on to anyone who’d listen: Someday soon, Georgia would be blue. This struck me as unlikely. But three years later Abrams ran for governor, and shocked the country by coming within two points of winning. Then two years later, when Joe Biden sealed his presidential election in 2020 with a win in Georgia, and Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff won Senate seats, Abrams looked prophetic. Now, Democrats have gone beyond Georgia, penetrating into the deepest reaches of the South—Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas. To understand how the GOP’s Solid South grew brittle, I could think of no better person to talk to than Abrams.

The following conversation has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Industry observers note that ta-Nehisi Coates: My recollection of our first meeting goes back to 2015, when I was promoting Between the World and Me. You interviewed me for the book. We had a wonderful discussion. My family was actually in the audience, because, like all Black folks, I have family in Atlanta. They were so excited. I was talking to Stacey Abrams—Minority Leader Stacey Abrams. And one of the things you said backstage was, “We’re going to make Georgia blue.” And I don’t know that I scoffed at you. I like to think I wasn’t quite that rude.

Stacey Abrams: Your eyebrow arched a bit.

It has been revealed that I confess to the eyebrow arching. And so the eyebrow arched and you made the case. Can you tell me what you saw?

Sources indicate that I’d gone through redistricting, and one of the component pieces of redistricting, of course, is that it’s predicated on the census. The US census is a tool that is incredibly powerful and deeply inexact. It was the first time Republicans had power to draw the lines since Reconstruction. And I took a posture in my caucus, and it was this: “If you vote for their maps, I will come after your seats.” And I was not only unequivocal in saying it, I wrote it down because I didn’t want anyone to misquote me.

Industry observers note that in order to take that posture, I had to read the maps myself. And what I saw was that Republicans were placing bets that, by drawing the lines a certain way, they were going to give themselves 124 of 180 seats. So 67% of the seats, even though they’d only won the election by 57%.

But I looked at those same maps and I’m like, In this place, in this part of Paulding County, there is a new subdivision that is predominantly Black. And in this part of Gwinnett County, there is a burgeoning Korean population that is now going into its second generation, which means a lot of those will be eligible voters. And down in South Georgia, you have third-generation migrant farm workers who are Latino, but who have decided to plant their roots here and raise their families here. When you looked at those numbers, the maps had a very different story to tell about Republican dominance: They could win for a decade. They could not win for a generation.

We tell ourselves stories about the information we get, and people repeat stories without ever reading it themselves. There are a lot of people who can quote Tom Sawyer who’ve never read the book. And so in our politics, that happens a lot, that the story that becomes popular doesn’t ever get traced back to its origin or to the original text.

What I saw in Georgia is true in Louisiana, in Mississippi, in Tennessee, in Alabama, in South Carolina. We just saw it happen in North Carolina.

So when you saw this wave of redistricting happening around the country this year, did you see a similar opportunity?

Oh, absolutely. I was in Tennessee the day that they passed the maps and what stuck out for me was Raumesh Akbari, who’s the Senate minority leader, she asked to see the bill, and the Republican chair of the committee said, “Well, we don’t have a bill yet, but we know what it’s going to say.” They planned to vote on it even though they did not have the text of the bill.

The Republicans were moving so fast because they thought they understood what they were pulling together. Justin Pearson didn’t pick up the seat he wanted, but they were at risk of losing a seat they thought was going to be theirs because they misread the topography, but they didn’t do a deeper dive into exactly what was laying in the crevices. And that’s where opportunity for us is born.

There are not enough Black people to win any single seat outright on their own in most legislative districts, and no statewide elections, especially post–Louisiana v. Callais, but there are coalitions that can be built. And what I saw from the very beginning was the possibility of coalition.

What I see for the South, what I think the South proved on Tuesday, is the possibility of coalition, but coalition does not happen without conflict. It does not happen without conversation, and it does not happen when we have convinced ourselves of the permanence of our second-class citizenship and our subjugation. What we saw on Tuesday was a moment where people realized that the power to improve their own lives had become so desperately thin that they had to use it or lose it. We cannot rely on that for the next two years.

What I hear you saying is that the last two years created an emergency. But that can’t be depended on. It can’t be “The Most Crucial Election of Our Lifetime” every two years. Desperation is not enough.

It can’t be. Desperation gets you one moment. There’s a whole body of medical research on people that have heart attacks and they get saved. And what it indicates is that they are exercise fiends for about six weeks and then they fall back into their patterns because it’s a normalcy bias.

If we constantly feel on the edge of danger, we cannot function. And so we reorient our understanding of normal to survive. And therefore our responsibility in this moment is to look at the opportunity that was revealed on Tuesday, but not read into it that that opportunity either requires desperation or it requires this milquetoast approach, because our default is not just normalcy, but the most banal form of normalcy we can imagine.

Recent findings suggest that I know you have some concerns about some of the narratives emerging out of the midterms. Would you talk a bit about that?

In a recent development, I saw something on Axios that I think was well-intentioned and it essentially stated that the threats to our democracy were overblown, that our courts held, that our Congress held, that our presidency wasn’t overreaching, and that for normal people, things were fine. How have we reached the place where we think it is normal that the capital city in the United States of America is under military occupation? How is it okay that the courts held when it permits the incarceration of children in Dilley, Texas, and the kidnapping of people of color because of race and the language that they speak? There is something aggressively privileged about this idea that democracy is not in jeopardy because those who are the most protected don’t feel harm.

But Tuesday was a repudiation of this idea that things are normal. You saw turnout at extraordinary levels from a cross section of communities, almost all of whom have been directly impacted by the harms of this administration. Not just the economic harms that hit everyone, but harms that were amplified and refined for their cruelty.

At the same time, there’s a worry that I have that, because we won control of Congress for the patriots—and that’s how I frame it, I no longer think it’s just Democrat versus Republican, it’s patriots versus authoritarians—even though the patriots may have gained more purchase in Congress, we still have a Supreme Court that gutted the last vestiges of protection for the Voting Rights Act. We still have a Supreme Court that stripped women of their bodily autonomy. We still have a Supreme Court that has said that protections that are afforded by DEI are somehow suspect. And when those are true, then the successes of Tuesday don’t signal that we’ve won. They signal that we have to work even harder because the harms have not dissipated, they just haven’t penetrated.

You mentioned something a few months back that’s stuck with me—that our elections are ripe for entertainment. As a sports fan, I think it’s not a coincidence that so many sports figures are now commenting on politics because the way they appear on TV is actually quite similar to the way sports appears. You have these long campaigns, which is like your season. Then you have primaries, which are like your playoffs, and then you have this massive Super Bowl that happens on Tuesday. And so, it’s an entertainment and ratings bonanza. And I think, as I recall, you were cautioning against that as a view of politics. Can you speak a little bit more about that?

Industry observers note that yeah. When you think about politics, if you think about elections as an event, and to extend your analogy, if the elections are the finals, if the elections are game seven, if it’s the Super Bowl, when that happens, then the day after, you go home, the game is over. But the challenge I have is that it’s not just that we treat it as a sporting event, it’s that we treat politics as though we are spectators at a sporting event. And when we look at the other party, it’s like we are spectators watching a very disciplined, seasoned team that practices in the off-season, that travels together, that plays overseas. They’re constantly engaged and we are on and off. We think of politics, again, as entertainment as opposed to the job.

How did we end up with this entertainment narrative?

Sources indicate that theodore White did this series where he examined elections 1960, 1964, 1968, 1972. And when you read it, as someone who is reading it in the 21st century, the arc of how we have viewed politics changed dramatically, specifically in 1960 with the advent of television, because the election contest between John Kennedy and Richard Nixon hinged in no small part on that televised debate. And I think for you and me and for anyone who wasn’t old enough to see it, I did not realize that it was one of the most watched programs in American history. We take for granted how many people are going to watch the debates these days, but with that first debate, it was one of the most watched programs in the world because it had never happened before. And the moment it became a television spectacle, it became entertainment because you were watching, you picked winners and losers, you picked your villain and you picked your champion.

Industry observers note that it’s human nature, we put things into these narrative arcs. As someone who writes comic books, you understand this. As someone who writes thrillers, I think about this. You create a villain, you have a protagonist, an antagonist, you have to have a storyline, you have to have complications, and when television became the medium, it added a layer and a texture to what had long been the mechanics of politics. Then you add into it the drama of Black and brown people getting to participate. And then you layer on top of that “blue state versus red state,” and the sharp division, and the attribution to entire regions of a value system and a personality based on a single day.

It has been revealed that what would it mean to remain engaged beyond elections? When I think about the conservative movement, I think about the degree to which the religious right is engaged. I think about Trump rallies. I think people were baffled by this at first—the clothes, the trucks, the boats. But what I would say is those are markers of community. They aren’t my politics. But they seem part of something larger than a particular bill or policy.

It has been revealed that there’s a lot of talk in organizing about going for belief first, or belonging first. On the left, we are often accused of belief, that you have to be in line with all of our ideas, our values, our ideologies, but also the tactical, practical ways of exercising them, and that because we say you have to believe first, we filter out people who haven’t had time to understand or adapt or even decide what they believe. The right uses belonging. They say, “Come and be a part of us, and we’ll tell you what we are.” So you get the jersey, you get the cap, you get the red, you get to use the language, even if you haven’t decided that you actually believe all they believe, which is why you have people who are suddenly surprised that this is what happened.

Sources indicate that we have to shift. Not to say that we don’t have beliefs, but we have to give people time to grow into those beliefs. I come at this from my time as minority leader. I had a caucus of 60 members in a chamber of 180, and my members included suburban white mothers and rural Black pastors and everything in between. We were the most racially diverse caucus. We were geographically diverse. And I had no power. I was the minority leader. My job was to help harmonize their approach. I could not lead with belief, because people were entitled to their beliefs, but my job was to bring them into belonging first because they were members of the caucus. And then my second job was to make sure that anyone who needed them to believe something had the platform to offer the tutelage.

According to recent reports, that’s the place where I think we are failing. We don’t do the tutelage. We say, “There has been a conversation, this is now our truth. And if you don’t adopt that truth, you are somehow opposed to it,” as opposed to, “You haven’t adopted the truth because you don’t know what it means and you don’t understand it and you haven’t experienced it. Let me give you time and space to come in,” or, “You have legitimate disagreement, and maybe on this, we will not be in alignment, but your disagreement should not lead to hostility against my community.”.

Sources indicate that the Democratic Socialists of America have attracted a lot of attention recently, but one thing they seem to do is this “belonging” piece. I can’t say I understood this before, but I was talking to someone for a story, and then mentioned the social environment. So here in New York, when people go out to canvas, afterwards, they all go out for beers. The beers are not really the point, but making people feel like they belong to something is.

Industry observers note that yeah. I mean, what they are doing is what works in most effective social movements. During the Vietnam War, one of the most effective protest waves happened at coffee shops. You brought people together around the table, they got to vent about what they were upset about, they went out and protested and then they came back together. People like being liked.

It has been revealed that in terms of belief, how does one do that and not make those who are in that coalition who are particularly vulnerable feel abandoned? Obviously, I mean, this is not the only case, but I’m thinking about the tremendous amount of negative attention brought on the trans community. What do you do when the “belonging” comes in conflict with actually protecting the members of your coalition?

It has been revealed that my first position is, if you have a faith that tells you it is okay to cause harm because you feel uncomfortable, I need to understand where your faith lies. Our first responsibility is the protection of difference. And it is to say you don’t have to embrace, but you cannot lift up pitchforks. You cannot demonize, you cannot revile, you cannot scapegoat because all of those are hostile actions of cruelty that not only cause harm to the victim, they diminish your ability to learn. So the worry I have is that too often we sacrifice that education piece because it’s uncomfortable and because it requires defending those you may not be in complete alignment with, and it’s an easier thing to just jump on the bandwagon.

It has been revealed that in my caucus, when I was a minority leader, another concern I had was abortion, and I had two members who were pastors. I was not going to be able to change their ideological position and I wasn’t going to try. But I had these members walk off the floor, instead of voting, on abortion bills. And there were some who got mad and they’re like, “Oh, we should know their position.” I mentioned, “A yes vote on this bill causes harm, and no vote is a help. Not voting is the same as a no vote. So why do you need them to make a declaration when their declaration of refusing to do harm is progress?” So there’s a complexity that we often elide because we failed to measure what harm looks like, and the path from good to harm is a lot shorter than we want to believe.

Did you work with Angie Nixon during her race?

I feel like she excited a certain element of the base in a way that we haven’t really seen before.

I contributed and then I went down to Florida, actually did an event at Florida A&M University and did one at Cafe Resistance. I got to know her mama. I knew of her as a state representative. And when I decided to support her campaign, it was because she has always put the work of serving people first. She has built networks, but more importantly, she solves problems.

It has been revealed that when Florida started banning books, she started a bookstore for banned books. That kind of tactical response with strategic intention is often lacking and it has been part of how I try to operate. We’ve got people who are good at being diagnosticians and we’ve got folks who can offer prescriptions and we’ve got people who can actually administer the medicine. And we need more people who are willing to do all three. You need people who are specialists; I’m not saying you don’t, but what she has demonstrated is the capacity to do the three.

Have you heard some of the negative commentary after the election about her campaign? I’m thinking about James Carville, for instance—this notion that somehow she was a poor fit for Florida or was a bad candidate. It’s not great. Have you seen any of this?

I have. I don’t read very much of it.

According to recent reports, well, I have thoughts on the fact that we keep thinking the solution to the problem is the thing that failed before. And I believe in experimentation. If you look at my history, I have never been top of mind as the solution to problems. And some of it is timing, some of it is capacity, and some of it is helping change the public imagination, but we’re never going to get what we need if we only use what we’ve always had.

According to recent reports, I just find it interesting that she is attracting negative commentary, from certain quarters, in a way that David Jolly is not, even though they both lost and the margin wasn’t that much between the two of them. She came very, very close to winning, in a state Democrats really didn’t expect to compete in two years ago. And look, I just have to say, you are somebody who in 2018 came really, really close too. You’re both Black women. I just wonder what you make of the critique.

Industry observers note that the critique is easy because Angie Nixon is different. She’s different than what they are used to, and she is different than 250 years of expectation has led us to presume is right. I am excited about Juliana Stratton and Angela Alsobrooks and Lisa Blunt Rochester being in the US Senate. That is an extraordinary thing. Adding Angie Nixon would’ve been an amazing, amazing addition. But for pundits whose sense of success is grounded in past history, she strains the imagination.

David Jolly ran a smart race. Angie Nixon ran a smart race, and we know that because they came close to winning, but you are never entitled to victory. You are entitled to effort. And this notion that there is some magical formula for what wins in the South got completely obliterated yesterday when Scott Colom won a seat that we haven’t held since 1874. We know that what can win is a combination of a smart candidate, an invested campaign, and an electorate who sees and hears themselves in the story told.

Angie didn’t get that opportunity because she had a late primary and no resources. And to judge her using a metric that was never designed for her is deeply problematic. And it’s not just about her being a Black woman, it’s about how do we win an evolving electorate if all we know is to do what we’ve always done? And so my argument for the Democratic Party is that our notions of electability have to evolve with the democracy that we deserve and that we design, and it cannot be anchored to these sometimes antiquated notions that the only thing we can do is not lose as opposed to let’s try really hard to win by meeting the moment. And I think Angie Nixon did an incredible job of meeting the moment.

And what about you—do you still have ambitions for public office?

Recent findings suggest that do you worry that some of the work you do as a kind of public political strategist (like in this interview, frankly) will conflict at all? When I think about people seeking office, they often try to say as little as possible.

Politics is a tool. It is not an identity for me. It’s a tool. And that’s different. And there are people for whom this is what they do and we need those people. This is not a disparaging comment about others, but for me, it is a tool. It is one of the ways to do the work I believe needs to be done. I think that poverty is immoral. I think it is solvable. I think it is economically inefficient. And for most of my life, the work for me has been about how do you solve this economic poverty? When I got deep in the work, I realized that we also had a moral poverty that we had to contend with, and we have this poverty of imagination. And the problem is you cannot convince people to believe that their problems can be solved if you won’t talk about them.

Sources indicate that and in the South, silence is protective. It has been a way to nibble around the edges, but the only people who could be loud about it were the people who could afford volume. And politicians rarely can afford volume. I want things to be better and I’m not willing to forgo any tool that will make that happen. But I’m also not willing to protect my future opportunities by rejecting my current responsibilities.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA games are major, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.
  • It has been revealed that naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats.
  • Industry observers note that maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Using cheats in GTA 6 is a given. GTA games are major, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.

It has been revealed that naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats. But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems:.

Industry observers note that maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so.

GTA 6 is a big, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu.

That's where I found the next bit of bad news...

It has been revealed that congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Most cheats on the menu are locked because there are requirements you need to meet to use them. Want a cheat that removes fall damage? First you'll need to survive 20 falls of over more than 40 feet. Want to spawn a parachute? First complete 50 skydives and basejumps.

Using an infinite ammo cheat means first winning 25 medals on shooting ranges. To fast-forward time you'll need to find 10 collectible watches—and in 90 hours I found exactly one of them. Spawning a jet means first completing every single challenge in the game, which is gonna take, ooh, let me check… forever.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I don't love this cheat unlock system at all, but there's even more bad news:.

Want to use a cheat to give yourself an extra $250,000 so you can go on a car buying spree? Cool, go ahead. But you won't be able to save your progress once you enable a cheat.

Industry observers note that whatever fun you have cheating is purely of the sandbox variety. You can buy cars and clothes and guns with cheated money, but you'll lose it all when you stop playing because you're not allowed to save your game once you use a single cheat. Booo.

And there's one final bummer for ya:.

It has been revealed that I tried it. I opened an older save where I hadn't yet completed the main story, and tried to input the cheats I'd learned from my complete game save. No dice! The cheats don't work unless you're using a save file that's story complete. So, starting over at the beginning and using cheats? Not gonna happen.

Sources indicate that I'm really not a fan of this. With so many restrictions in place, Rockstar has really taken the fun out of being a huge GTA cheater! When GTA 6 finally comes to PC, I hope modders make cheats their top priority.

CameoGTA 3GTA 6Rob NelsonRockstar GamesSam Houser.

Grand Theft Auto 6 contains some surprising and fun cameos and moments, including what appears to be a strange appearance by Rockstar Games co-founder and manufacturer president Sam Houser. I asked Rockstar about this cameo and got some laughs and (mostly) confirmation that it’s him in the game.

During a pre-release interview with Rockstar’s head of production Rob Nelson, who acted as basically the director behind GTA 6, I asked a lot of questions about things I found while playing the newly released open-world sequel for over 150 hours. And I had to ask about a strange cameo that happens late in the middle half of the game’s main story. An older man appears wearing a shirt featuring the Rockstar Games logo. He’s called Little Sam and doesn’t say anything. All signs pointed to this being Sam Houser.

So I asked Nelson about this cameo and got a laugh from him and Rockstar PR in the Zoom chat.

“Little Sam?” replied Nelson with a smirk. “I mean, I can’t I can confirm or deny it. I think it’ll be very interesting when fans see that.” Nelson then laughed more. I pointed out that Sam Houser had a voice cameo as a gun store clerk in GTA 3, something Nelson was well aware of, and so it seemed very likely this was him. Little Sam looks a lot like Houser in this recent pic posted online a year ago.

“[He was in GTA 3,] so I wouldn’t be surprised if that’s him. I wouldn’t be surprised,” playfully responded Nelson. “That’s little Sam; his name is little Sam. He don’t say much.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the Newly introduced Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Recent findings suggest that for those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

It has been revealed that microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too. If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's major release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.
